Four ML models (XGBoost, SVM, logistic regression, ANN) are trained and compared on real versus CTGAN-synthesized data, finding no significant performance difference for synthesis but degraded performance when CTGAN is used for class-imbalance augmentation. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN with its mode-specific normalization and conditional vector, is run directly as the sole synthetic data generator underpinning the entire empirical study.
paper-synthetic-driven-learning-iomt-202.needs: Evidence does not confirm whether the SDV-dev ctgan package was used directly or an authors' own implementation; described architecture matches the standard CTGAN design and cites the original GitHub repo, suggesting library use, but no explicit import/package statement is given.

paper-ctgan-synthetic-generation-low-202.summary: This IEEE PES General Meeting paper proposes a pipeline that maps low-voltage distribution network topology graphs (via ResNet50 feature extraction and PCA) into synthetic node, feeder, and cable data to overcome data scarcity and privacy limits in LV network modeling. The generated data is validated with JSD, MMD, Coverage and Precision metrics against real UK LV network data, comparing CTGAN, TVAE, and cGAN outputs. CTGAN is run directly via SDV's CTGANSynthesizer (v1.2.0) as the primary generator producing the synthetic LV network data underlying the whole evaluation.
paper-ctgan-synthetic-generation-low-202.needs: TVAE results are also reported (Table I); unclear whether TVAE was likewise run through SDV's TVAESynthesizer or a separate implementation, though the same 'from SDV' sentence suggests it was.

paper-scoping-review-privacy-utility-202.summary: This is a scoping review that systematizes methods used in the literature to evaluate the privacy and utility of synthetic health-related data, finding no consensus on utility metrics and widespread underestimation of privacy risks. It surveys existing open-source tooling and generator methods reported across included studies rather than running experiments itself. Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is named among several open-source platforms said to let researchers create and measure synthetic data quality, cited only in passing as one such tool.
paper-scoping-review-privacy-utility-202.needs: Full author affiliations not visible in provided text excerpts (footnote numbers 1 and 2 given but institution names not shown); CopulaGan appears in a figure-derived word list of methods used across reviewed studies but is not clearly attributed to the authors' own use, so left out of sdv_concept.

paper-access-denied-meaningful-access-20.summary: This CHI 2025 paper studies how restricted data access degrades the reliability of algorithmic fairness audits, running simulated audits on recidivism and healthcare-coverage prediction datasets under three levels of data access. To test how the choice of synthetic data generator affects metric reliability, the authors generate audit datasets using the Gaussian Copula Synthesizer, CTGAN Synthesizer, and Copula-GAN Synthesizer from the Synthetic Data Vault library, alongside PrivBayes as a differential-privacy baseline. SDV's GaussianCopula, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN synthesizers are run as parallel synthetic-data generators whose outputs are compared for their effect on fairness-metric estimation accuracy.

paper-calibrated-mixup-imbalanced-regres.summary: This paper addresses imbalanced regression on tabular data, proposing a calibrated mixup technique to improve prediction performance when target values are unevenly distributed. It cites CTGAN as related work in the space of generative approaches for tabular data. No further detail on how CTGAN is used is available from the metadata alone.
paper-calibrated-mixup-imbalanced-regres.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is run, used as baseline, or merely cited in related work discussion.

paper-mtabgen-diffusion-2025.summary: Proposes MTabGen, a diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data that makes three changes to TabDDPM: an encoder-decoder transformer replaces the MLP denoiser, the conditioning features reach the decoder through the attention mechanism as key and value rather than by adding their embedding to the masked features, and the split between conditioned and masked columns is redrawn per row during training, so one model covers both synthetic data generation and missing-value imputation. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generative baselines it is measured against across ten datasets, run from the SDV distribution and tuned under the same Bayesian search budget as the diffusion models.

paper-energydiff-universal-time-series-2.summary: This paper proposes EnergyDiff, a diffusion-model-based framework for generating high-resolution synthetic energy time-series data (electricity demand, heat pump, PV), introducing a denoising network and a Marginal Calibration technique, and shows improvements over baselines across multiple resolutions and domains. The vine copula (t-Copula) method from the SDV family is cited only as an example of a conventional statistical generative approach that the paper contrasts with its deep generative diffusion model, without being run or benchmarked.

paper-enhancing-patient-centric-syntheti.summary: This conference paper presents a patient-centric, statistics-based methodology for generating synthetic Chronic Kidney Disease patient records from the MIMIC-III dataset, emphasizing explainability over AI-based approaches. The authors compare their method's output against synthetic data produced by SMOTE and, more extensively, against Gaussian Copula and CTGAN synthesizers. The SDV library's Gaussian Copula and CTGAN algorithms are run directly to generate comparison synthetic datasets that are benchmarked against the authors' own methodology across multiple CKD stages.
paper-enhancing-patient-centric-syntheti.needs: Only metadata was available (no abstract, no citing sentences, no full text); cannot confirm whether SDV/CTGAN etc. were actually run as part of the comparative analysis or merely cited as background. Integration and importance are best guesses pending fuller evidence.

paper-gtv-generating-tabular-vertical-20.summary: This paper proposes GTV, a framework for training tabular GANs across vertically partitioned data held by different organizations using Vertical Federated Learning, with a training-with-shuffling technique to prevent reconstruction of training data from the GAN's conditional vector. The authors evaluate GTV's synthetic data quality, scalability, and robustness to membership inference attacks under differential privacy across multiple datasets. GTV's generator and discriminator architecture is built by mirroring CTGAN's design, adopting its mode-specific normalization, one-hot encoding, and conditional vector construction method into their own distributed reimplementation rather than running the sdv-dev package.
paper-gtv-generating-tabular-vertical-20.needs: GTV builds its own reimplementation of CTGAN's architecture into a federated framework; whether this counts as derivative_work or port is a close call since the base techniques are reimplemented but composed into a genuinely new distributed model with a novel shuffling defense.

paper-gait-stability-prediction-syntheti.summary: This study proposes a data-centric synthetic data generation (SDG) approach for predicting the Margin of Stability (MoS) in older adults, combining constraint-based synthetic time-series generation with smartphone-based, MediaPipe computer-vision gait analysis to address data scarcity in vulnerable populations. Using a public dataset of 14 older adults, the authors generated synthetic gait data via SDV with metadata configuration and rank-correlation constraints, and a model trained solely on this synthetic data (TSTR) outperformed one trained on real data. SDV is run as the generator producing the synthetic gait dataset underlying the whole empirical study, with SDMetrics (KSComplement, TVComplement) used to evaluate its fidelity.

paper-informative-instances-more-importa.summary: This conference paper addresses class imbalance in postoperative pulmonary complication (PPC) prediction by proposing feature-level and instance-level hard-constraint modules that filter GAN-generated synthetic samples to remove medically invalid or uninformative instances. The data generation module uses CTGAN to synthesize tabular patient data, which is then post-processed by the hard-constraint pipeline before being used to augment PPC prediction model training. CTGAN is run as the generator producing the raw synthetic samples that the whole proposed pipeline filters and evaluates.
paper-informative-instances-more-importa.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run as a baseline or only discussed in related work.

paper-mitigating-potential-risk-counterf.summary: This paper proposes a method for generating counterfactual explanations to identify and mitigate risk factors in blast-based tunnel construction, aiming to improve interpretability of risk-prediction models used in this domain. The metadata indicates it cites the CTGAN paper, but no abstract or full text was available to establish how CTGAN's generative model is actually used in the pipeline. CTGAN is cited, with its role in the work otherwise unverifiable from the available evidence.
paper-mitigating-potential-risk-counterf.needs: Full text and abstract not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run (e.g., to generate counterfactual or synthetic samples) or only cited as related work in this tunnel-construction risk paper.

paper-multitable-gap-2025.summary: Asks why a transformer relational synthesiser trails a diffusion one on multi-table data when the two are close on single tables, and attributes the difference to how each represents contextual information and the parent-child link. Two changes close much of the gap: tying the transformer block weights of the parent model to the relational adapter's decoder so only the child vocabulary is fine-tuned, and inserting a cluster identifier as an in-context categorical cue in both tables, an autoregressive stand-in for classifier guidance. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the single-table baselines it benchmarks, and CTGAN is described as the GAN adaptation that handles heterogeneous columns and class imbalance.

paper-prediction-chloride-resistance-sea.summary: A materials-engineering paper proposing a GAN-based data-generation step combined with a stacking ensemble learning model to predict the chloride resistance of seawater sea sand concrete, likely to address limited experimental data for this niche material. The metadata indicates the work cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, but no abstract or citing sentence is available to confirm how CTGAN's method is actually used. CTGAN is cited in connection with the generative adversarial network component of the proposed prediction pipeline, though whether it was run, adapted, or merely referenced cannot be confirmed from this evidence.
paper-prediction-chloride-resistance-sea.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run to generate synthetic concrete data or only cited as prior GAN work. Integration and true importance remain uncertain.

paper-frp-strengthened-columns-2025.summary: Builds predictive models for the axial capacity of FRP-strengthened concrete columns, where design codes leave the effectiveness of fibres under compression uncertain. 112 experimental samples are paired one-for-one with 112 TGAN-generated ones, an unusually explicit statement of how far the synthetic half of a training set extends.

paper-privacy-computation-trade-offs-202.summary: This theory paper on differential privacy studies Private Repetition and metaselection algorithms that boost the success probability of differentially private algorithms, proving lower bounds showing failure probability can only fall polynomially (not exponentially) with computational overhead, and gives near-matching hybrid algorithms. CTGAN is mentioned only as an illustrative example of a computationally expensive private learning algorithm (training a CTGAN via DPSGD or PATE) that motivates the privacy-computation tradeoff, not as something run or evaluated in the paper.

paper-regression-tools-chemical-release-.summary: This paper evaluates several regression methods (linear least squares, LASSO, Ridge, decision trees, random forest, neural networks) for predicting chemical releases during extrusion-based additive manufacturing, using curated secondary data on polymeric extrusion. It also explores whether adding synthetic data/noise to the dataset can improve regression performance. The synthetic data generation approach is attributed to the SDV framework (Patki et al. 2016), cited as the source method for generating synthetic samples to augment the training dataset.
paper-regression-tools-chemical-release-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software was actually run (api_user) or only cited as the conceptual source for synthetic data generation, nor which specific SDV algorithm/component was used.

paper-safesql-llm-synthetic-privacy-2025.summary: Proposes a hybrid Text-to-SQL framework in which a local LLM generates synthetic table rows that statistically mimic sensitive data, sharing only schema and vetted synthetic rows with a cloud LLM for SQL generation, evaluated on the Spider benchmark. The paper cites CTGAN alongside another reference as prior work on generating fabricated rows from schema and statistics, but its own synthetic rows are produced by an LLM rather than by running CTGAN or any SDV tool. CTGAN is mentioned only as a citation for the general idea of synthetic row generation, with no SDV code, package, or model actually used.
paper-safesql-llm-synthetic-privacy-2025.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed further beyond this single citation or if it informs the synthetic row generation design in any deeper way.

paper-synthetic-generation-enhanced-mode.summary: This conference paper studies the use of CTGAN to generate synthetic tabular data and evaluates how augmenting real training data with CTGAN-generated samples affects the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting classifiers, using paired t-tests to validate significance. The authors preprocess a mixed numerical/categorical dataset, train CTGAN with a specified architecture (256 hidden units, learning rate 0.0002, 70 epochs), and explicitly run it via a Python library alongside Scikit-learn and Pandas. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is the sole generator producing the synthetic data underpinning the entire empirical evaluation.
paper-synthetic-generation-enhanced-mode.needs: Underlying dataset domain (e.g., a 'MonthlyCharges' feature suggests telecom churn) is not explicitly named in the evidence, so industry is set to cross_industry rather than a specific vertical.

paper-tabfairgdt-fast-fair-tabular-2025.summary: This paper introduces TabFairGDT, a lightweight, CPU-efficient fair synthetic tabular data generator based on autoregressive decision trees with a soft leaf resampling technique to reduce bias while preserving utility. It is proposed as an alternative to deep generative models, reporting large speedups and improved fairness-utility trade-offs on benchmark fairness datasets. CTGAN is cited in the related-work discussion as an example of a GAN-based tabular data generator that the authors' non-parametric approach departs from.
paper-tabfairgdt-fast-fair-tabular-2025.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE are actually run as baselines in the experimental comparison against SOTA deep generative models, which would raise integration to baseline_only and importance to 3-4.

paper-understanding-water-consumption-se.summary: This study analyzes shower duration, timing, and day-of-week patterns among university students at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, comparing them to single-family residential shower habits to inform tailored water conservation strategies. Facing limited sample size, the authors used Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks to generate synthetic data to validate their empirical findings. CTGAN is run as the synthetic data generator used to confirm the robustness of the study's shower-behavior results.
paper-understanding-water-consumption-se.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run or a custom reimplementation was used, so integration is marked unclear.

paper-radiomics-privacy-preserving-synth.summary: Treats a radiomic signature as identifying in itself and tests whether synthetic radiomics can carry prostate-cancer aggressiveness classification instead, on 4,588 retrospective and 1,369 prospective mpMRI cases from 12 EU centres. Three generators compete — a custom Bayesian Gaussian Mixture variant, CTGAN and TVAE — and the custom BGMMOCE wins on Jensen-Shannon divergence and Hellinger distance. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the three compared arms and are named as methods, not as a library, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.
paper-radiomics-privacy-preserving-synth.needs: IEEE Xplore is paywalled to automated fetches; confirm whether CTGAN and TVAE came from SDV. The same group's other work in this index may settle it.

paper-hybrid-resampling-address-class-20.summary: This paper proposes RAMGANH, a hybrid resampling method for class-imbalanced datasets that combines a Heuristic Range-Based Association rule for undersampling the majority class with a customized/modified Tabular Generative Adversarial Network for oversampling the minority class. The method is evaluated with SVM classifiers on several standard imbalanced datasets, showing improvements over other state-of-the-art resampling techniques. TGAN, the tabular GAN from Xu and Veeramachaneni (2018), is modified and combined with the association-rule component to form the core generator of the proposed hybrid approach.
paper-hybrid-resampling-address-class-20.needs: Unclear whether 'modified TGAN' reuses any sdv-dev/TGAN code or is a from-scratch reimplementation of the architecture; no library import or code details are given in the visible text.

paper-generalised-extreme-value-gradient.summary: This paper proposes GEV-GBDT, a gradient boosting decision tree that replaces the logistic sigmoid activation with the asymmetric cumulative distribution function of the generalised extreme value distribution, to better handle class imbalance in credit scoring. Tested on four real-life loan datasets, it outperforms SMOTE and cost-sensitive baselines, especially under extreme imbalance ratios. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as one of several 'advanced generalisation models' used for imbalanced data in related work, without being run in the experiments.
paper-generalised-extreme-value-gradient.needs: Full text not available; only abstract and citing sentence seen, so it's unclear whether CTGAN is discussed further or used empirically anywhere in the paper.

paper-ready-multimodal-pipeline-enrich-2.summary: This paper presents an AI-ready multimodal data integration pipeline that combines structured EHR data, clinical notes, and imaging data to predict radiation therapy interruptions in cancer patients. Due to small sample size and patient privacy concerns, the authors generate a 5,000-record synthetic dataset used for training and validating their RTI prediction model. CTGAN is run directly to learn the joint distribution of the structured dataset and produce the synthetic patient records that form the training data for the case study.
paper-ready-multimodal-pipeline-enrich-2.needs: Full text not obtained; unable to confirm how central CTGAN-generated synthetic data is to the overall pipeline's empirical results or whether it is evaluated against other generators.

paper-advancing-organizational-science-s.summary: This is a methods/tutorial paper introducing organizational scientists to machine-learning-based synthetic data generation, proposing a systematic framework for creating and evaluating synthetic datasets and presenting two empirical demonstrations using GAN-based synthetic data on workplace assessment datasets. The authors explicitly generate their synthetic data using the Python SDV package and select CTGAN as the generative model, tuning hyperparameters such as epoch and batch size across both studies. SDV's package (via CTGAN) is run directly as the generator underlying both empirical demonstrations that form the paper's core contribution.
paper-advancing-organizational-science-s.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear which specific SDV synthesizer (e.g., GaussianCopula) was invoked, and whether CTGAN/CopulaGAN were run or only discussed as related methods.

paper-empirical-machine-learning-synthet.summary: This paper empirically compares five machine-learning-based synthetic job trace generation methods (vanilla GAN, CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, and CopulaGAN) against a manual statistical baseline (Lublin model), evaluating them across CDF plots, statistical distance metrics, and simulation-based scheduling on real-world HPC job traces. The study finds that TVAE, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN consistently outperform vanilla GAN and the manual statistical model in fidelity and downstream scheduling utility. CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula, and CopulaGAN -- all part of the SDV family -- are run as evaluation subjects across the whole empirical programme, comprising the core comparison of the paper.
paper-empirical-machine-learning-synthet.needs: Evidence does not explicitly confirm whether the SDV/ctgan Python packages were imported directly versus a custom implementation, though the presence of CopulaGAN strongly implies the SDV library API was used.

paper-causality-aware-local-interpretabl.summary: The paper proposes calime, an extension of LIME that replaces LIME's random local sampling with a causality-aware synthetic data generator, gencda, to produce more faithful and causally consistent explanations of black-box classifiers. Experiments compare calime's synthetic neighborhoods against the original data using outlier-detection and statistical fidelity indicators. To assess how well the generated synthetic neighborhood matches the real data, the authors adopt the statistical quality measures (e.g. GMLogLikelihood, KSTest, ContinuousKLDivergence) described in the SDV paper, applying SDV's synthetic-data evaluation methodology as part of their own experimental pipeline.

paper-driven-estimates-strength-failure-.summary: This paper applies the CTGAN method to generate synthetic data augmenting a limited experimental dataset on CFRP-steel bonded joints, aiming to improve data-driven estimation of joint strength and failure modes. It appears to use CTGAN as a data augmentation tool to overcome small-sample limitations in structural engineering datasets. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is used as the generator to synthesize training data for the estimation models.
paper-driven-estimates-strength-failure-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run or a custom reimplementation was used, so integration marked unclear.

paper-designing-evaluation-chain-assessi.summary: This conference paper builds and evaluates a pipeline for assessing the quality, fidelity, and utility of synthetic tabular healthcare data generated by GANs, using a public Kaggle heart-disease dataset. The authors train the CTGAN model to generate synthetic patient records and use SDMetrics to score resemblance via Column Shapes and Column Pair Trends metrics, explicitly noting both libraries are part of the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) project. CTGAN is run as the sole generator and SDMetrics as the sole evaluation tool, making SDV's tabular GAN and quality-scoring components the load-bearing empirical core of the study.
paper-designing-evaluation-chain-assessi.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so exact experimental role and depth of CTGAN/SDMetrics use could not be fully verified.

paper-enhanced-diabetes-detection-blood-.summary: This paper develops a TinyML-integrated electronic-nose system that analyzes exhaled breath volatile organic compounds to detect diabetes and predict blood glucose level, achieving 94.14% accuracy in diabetes detection with Random Forest and 86% accuracy in BGL identification with LightGBM. To overcome the small original sample of 58 participants, the authors used CTGAN to generate synthetic breath-sensor data, expanding the dataset to over 14,000 samples used to train and validate the machine learning models. CTGAN is run as the generator producing the synthetic samples that underpin the entire empirical evaluation, described mathematically as a generator/discriminator adversarial network rather than tied to a named library.
paper-enhanced-diabetes-detection-blood-.needs: Cannot determine from the evidence whether the authors ran the sdv-dev CTGAN package or built their own implementation from the described generator/discriminator equations; integration marked unclear.

paper-principle-practice-vertical-minimi.summary: This paper proposes vertical data minimization (vDM), a workflow based on data generalization that ensures no full-resolution client data is collected during ML training or deployment, and introduces Privacy-aware Tree (PAT), an algorithm that outperforms baseline vDM methods across several settings. The paper contrasts its generalization-based approach against the synthetic data setting as an alternative privacy-preserving paradigm. TGAN and CTGAN are cited only as examples of the synthetic data generation literature the authors position their work against, with no evidence either was run.
paper-principle-practice-vertical-minimi.needs: The whole text was searched and confirms no SDV-family term appears outside the reference list/contrastive citation, so this is bibliographic only.

paper-high-fidelity-cellular-network-202.summary: This paper proposes CPT-GPT, a transformer-based generative model for synthesizing high-fidelity mobile-core-network control-plane traffic without relying on domain-specific encoding schemes, addressing limitations of prior GAN-based traffic generators that ignore temporal and stateful semantics. The authors evaluate CPT-GPT against SMM and prior GAN-based traffic synthesis approaches on a large-scale control-plane trace. CTGAN is cited only in passing as one of several GAN-based prior-art approaches said to ignore temporal aspects and yield suboptimal fidelity relative to NetShare; it is not run or benchmarked in this work.

paper-identifying-handling-bias-within-2.summary: This paper proposes probabilistic methods to detect difficult-to-predict, under-represented data samples in ground truth healthcare data and to boost them when applying a synthetic data generator (using Bayesian networks), aiming to reduce bias while maintaining predictive performance. It is evaluated on primary care datasets to explore bias-reduction strategies for synthetic patient data. The SDV paper is cited only once in the introduction as a general example of generative models built from real data, with no SDV component run in the study.

paper-implementing-hierarchical-deep-lea.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical deep generative modeling methodology for simulating realistic first-price sealed-bid auction data, combining a tabular generator for auction/bidder features with a neural 'Bidnet' component that predicts the conditional bid distribution to address the multilevel structure of auctions. The authors train and compare two generators, CTGAN and TVAE, on their auction dataset, tuning CTGAN hyperparameters such as embedding dimensions, generator/discriminator dimensions, learning rates and decay rates, and evaluate synthetic data fidelity with classifiers trained on real versus synthetic data. CTGAN, run as SDV's conditional tabular GAN, outperformed TVAE in their experiments and is highlighted as the superior generator for this auction-simulation task.
paper-implementing-hierarchical-deep-lea.needs: Not fully certain whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev package or a custom reimplementation, though the hyperparameter names strongly match the SDV constructor API.

paper-cvd-risk-fs-ctgan-2024.summary: Predicts cardiovascular risk in diabetic patients by pairing feature selection with generated data, keeping the model interpretable enough to inspect. The published code is released as cvd-risk-fs-ctgan, naming CTGAN as the generator behind the oversampling the paper describes.
paper-cvd-risk-fs-ctgan-2024.needs: the body describes the oversampling as GAN-based without naming CTGAN in prose; the attribution rests on the repository name and the reference list

paper-leveraging-tabular-gans-malicious-.summary: This paper addresses classification of malicious addresses in the Ethereum blockchain network, an inherently class-imbalanced problem, by exploring tabular generative adversarial network approaches to model and augment address-feature data. Based on the title and citation, tabular GAN methods are applied to help distinguish malicious from benign addresses. The work cites CTGAN as a tabular GAN method relevant to its approach, though the exact role it plays (generator vs. baseline) cannot be confirmed from the available evidence.
paper-leveraging-tabular-gans-malicious-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot verify whether CTGAN is run directly (api_user), reimplemented (port), or only cited as related work. Industry classification between cybersecurity and finance_insurance is uncertain given only the title.

paper-measuring-classifying-usage-scenar.summary: This paper addresses IP usage scenario classification, proposing a deep continuous neural tree-based ensemble model to classify IP addresses into categories like home broadband, private enterprise, cellular network, and data center using network measurement features. The model captures higher-order feature interactions and generalizes across regions, evaluated on data from four large-scale regions. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-optimizing-industry-machine-learni.summary: This paper evaluates several Deep Generative Models—CTGAN, WGAN, TVAE, and TabDDPM—for augmenting an imbalanced gearbox-fault dataset from Bonfiglioli's EVO manufacturing plant, comparing synthetic data quality metrics and downstream classifier performance against SMOTE and ADASYN. CTGAN emerges as the best-performing model on classification metrics while TVAE also performs strongly on distributional similarity. The authors explicitly run CTGAN and TVAE through the SDV Python library, using its metadata API to configure the synthesizers on the industrial dataset.
paper-optimizing-industry-machine-learni.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev library or reimplemented, nor whether results tables include them as evaluation subjects.

paper-pdap-gan-generative-adversarial-20.summary: This paper proposes PDAP-GAN, a GAN-based model for anonymizing power-grid data that parses mixed-type JSON records with custom feature encoders and adds noise-based privacy protection during generation, aiming to preserve machine-learning utility and statistical similarity to the original data. It benchmarks its results against CT-GAN- and TableGAN-based generation models on classification utility and distributional similarity metrics. The paper adopts the mode-specific normalization concept from the CTGAN paper for its own continuous-variable encoder and compares its output against a CT-GAN-based baseline model.
paper-pdap-gan-generative-adversarial-20.needs: Unclear whether the CT-GAN baseline was implemented via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented from scratch; no import or constructor parameters are mentioned, so it is treated as an authors' own reimplementation (port).

paper-privatectgan-adapting-gan-privacy-.summary: This paper proposes PCTGAN, a privacy-aware variant of CTGAN that adds a privacy term to the generator's loss function to let users trade off data fidelity against privacy. The authors empirically compare PCTGAN against the original CTGAN and DP-CTGAN across ten public classification datasets, measuring predictive utility (AUC) and privacy/fidelity metrics. CTGAN's generator architecture and loss are directly extended with a new privacy-weighted loss term, making CTGAN the model being modified into the paper's proposed method.
paper-privatectgan-adapting-gan-privacy-.needs: Citation [20] used for CTGAN is actually Xu & Veeramachaneni's 2018 TGAN arXiv paper, not the CTGAN 2019 paper; a common mis-citation in this literature, recorded as given rather than corrected.

paper-synthetic-diffusion-models-improve.summary: This paper proposes Syngand, a diffusion GNN model that jointly generates ligand structures and pharmacokinetic property data end-to-end, aiming to address data sparsity in drug discovery datasets. The authors show that Syngand-generated synthetic target property data improves downstream regression performance on AqSolDB, LD50, and hERG Central benchmarks. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as an example of mode-specific normalization to alleviate mode collapse, with no code run or comparison made.

paper-synthetic-electrical-load-generati.summary: This conference paper generates synthetic electricity consumption data for Panama using TabGAN, a GAN variant proposed by Ashrapov (2020) that is distinct from CTGAN, and evaluates the synthetic data via descriptive statistics and by training MLP and LSTM load-forecasting models on augmented versus original data. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only once in the introduction as background on the general value of synthetic data for the electricity market, with no CTGAN code or model run anywhere in the study.
paper-synthetic-electrical-load-generati.needs: Full text needed to determine whether the paper's 'TabGAN' model is actually the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation, a reimplementation, or an unrelated architecture; the abstract does not clarify this.

paper-synthetic-reef-modelling-2024.summary: This paper presents a synthetic data generation pipeline built for ADRIA, a decision-support system for reef intervention scenarios on the Great Barrier Reef, allowing modelling results to be shared and published without disclosing sensitive site-specific data to stakeholders and rightsholders. The pipeline is showcased as a way to demonstrate models and methods to the reef decision-support community ahead of formal stakeholder discussions. It uses methods from the Python package Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al., 2016), among others, as the generator underlying the synthetic data pipeline.
paper-synthetic-reef-modelling-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; no specific SDV synthesizer or component (e.g., GaussianCopula, CTGAN) is named in the available evidence, only the package itself.

paper-synthetic-datasets-open-software-2.summary: This paper presents SynthMD, an open-source Python tool that generates synthetic rare-disease patient datasets (Sickle Cell Disease, Cystic Fibrosis, Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy) using a hierarchical, statistics-parameterised generation approach rather than learning from real patient data, drawing on US Census and CDC prevalence/demographic figures with the Faker library for individual records. The datasets and code are released as open data/software to support testing and privacy-technology development in rare disease research. SDV is cited only in passing as a data-generation tool learned from an existing database, explicitly noted as unsuited to the authors' scenario.

paper-tabularfm-open-framework-tabular-2.summary: This paper introduces TabularFM, an open-source framework for pretraining and benchmarking tabular foundational models across a thousand curated tabular datasets (GitTables and Kaggle), covering GAN-, VAE-, and Transformer-based architectures. Its core empirical programme pretrains CTGAN and TVAE, and introduces new variants (STVAE, STVAEM) that modify TVAE's architecture to improve cross-dataset transferability, evaluating outputs with column-shape and column-pair-trend similarity scores resembling SDMetrics' quality report. CTGAN and TVAE, the neural synthesizers from the SDV/CTGAN family, are pretrained, benchmarked, and structurally extended (via STVAE/STVAEM) as the paper's central generative models.
paper-tabularfm-open-framework-tabular-2.needs: IBM Research affiliation merges two distinct sites (Yorktown Heights, US and Dublin, Ireland) under one organization string per the naming rule; country was set to United States (majority) though one author is Dublin-based. Also unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev CTGAN package or reimplemented from scratch, though hyperparameter tables (network size, learning rate) and MIT-licensed model artifacts suggest use of the original package.

paper-transferable-neural-network-method.summary: This paper proposes a transfer-learning method for estimating permanent magnet temperature in PMSM electric drive systems, combining a 1-D CNN with a domain adaptation module so a pre-trained model can migrate across different motors without labeled target data. To strengthen the pre-training model's generalization before transfer, the authors augment their historical temperature sensor data using a GAN-based technique they call CTGAN, adept at generating one-dimensional tabular data. CTGAN is run as the data-augmentation generator that produces the synthetic training data feeding the pre-training stage of their pipeline.
paper-transferable-neural-network-method.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented from scratch; no library name, import, or constructor parameters are given, so api_user vs port is ambiguous.

paper-coronary-virtual-population-2023.summary: Compares five techniques for building virtual patient populations to augment clinical research databases that are short of subjects. Four of the five are SDV's, Tabular Preset, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and a CTGAN variant, so the comparison is largely internal to the library.

paper-fct-gan-enhancing-global-2023.summary: This paper proposes FCT-GAN, a conditional tabular GAN that incorporates Fourier Network Blocks alongside a CNN-based transformer-style tokenizer to better capture global column correlations and achieve permutation-invariant training for tabular data synthesis. It is evaluated against seven state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers across multiple real-world datasets, showing improved machine learning utility and statistical similarity. CTGAN (cited as CT-GAN) and TVAE are run as two of the seven baseline synthesizers, and CTGAN's conditional-vector design is described in related work as prior art the new architecture builds upon.
paper-fct-gan-enhancing-global-2023.needs: Unclear whether CT-GAN and TVAE baselines were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or via the authors' own reimplementation (as in their earlier CTAB-GAN codebase); no import or package name is given in the extracted text.

paper-generating-pseudo-random-volumes-2.summary: This paper presents an open-source modular system for procedurally generating synthetic volumetric datasets for VR/AR user studies, addressing the difficulty and expense of obtaining real volumetric data (e.g., from MRI/CT). It focuses on generating and validating volumes for immersive interaction studies rather than tabular data synthesis. SDV is cited only in passing as an example of prior work that creates randomly generated synthetic data from a smaller original dataset, with no SDV code run or adopted.
paper-generating-pseudo-random-volumes-2.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available. No evidence SDV software was run -- this is an off-domain (VR/AR volumetric data) paper citing SDV only as related prior art on synthetic data generation.

paper-hybrid-framework-generating-struct.summary: This paper presents an industry framework for generating synthetic relational (multi-table) data that preserves referential integrity, combining five configurable modeling approaches -- Gaussian Copula, TGAN, CTGAN, CopulaGAN and TVAE -- layered on top of the Hierarchical Modeling Algorithm (HMA), plus a Veracity/Variety/Volume evaluation module. The authors explicitly state they used the sdv package (version 0.17.1) with HMA as the backbone synthesizer and swapped in the other table-level generative models within it. SDV's relational HMA algorithm and its bundled Gaussian Copula, CopulaGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run directly as the core generative engine of the whole framework, with CTGAN and TGAN also executed and compared as alternative table-level models.
paper-hybrid-framework-generating-struct.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether HMA/GAN components are run via the SDV/TGAN libraries themselves (api_user) or reimplemented independently (port/derivative_work).

paper-predicting-iot-distributed-ledger-.summary: This paper proposes VecGAN, a lightweight GAN-based data augmentation method for predicting fraudulent transactions in resource-constrained IoT distributed ledger (blockchain) networks, aiming to replace computationally intensive Proof-of-Work consensus with machine-learning classification. VecGAN combines error-driven learning with Bayesian estimation and a dual-purpose discriminator to handle rare double-spend fraud events under class imbalance, improving classifier accuracy over other augmentation baselines while reducing computation. CTGAN was tested as a comparison baseline but was rejected after performing poorly on large datasets with long training times and high computation.
paper-predicting-iot-distributed-ledger-.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a reimplementation, and whether conditional_sampling concept applies.

paper-ctgan-differentially-private-medic.summary: This paper proposes DP-CTGAN, a variant of the conditional tabular GAN that incorporates differential privacy via gradient clipping and calibrated noise injection to generate synthetic medical tabular data, and further extends it into a federated-learning variant (FDP-CTGAN) to avoid centralizing sensitive patient data. The authors benchmark their model against PATE-GAN, DPGAN, and a non-private CTGAN baseline on several medical datasets, showing DP-CTGAN outperforms prior privacy-preserving GAN methods. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are directly built upon and modified to add differential-privacy training, with CTGAN itself also run unmodified as a non-private baseline.
paper-ctgan-differentially-private-medic.needs: Full text not obtained; only metadata/title available. Cannot confirm from text whether CTGAN was reimplemented (port) versus modified from the original sdv-dev codebase (derivative_work), though the title strongly implies CTGAN's architecture is directly extended.

paper-dpview-differentially-private-synt.summary: This paper proposes DPView, an automated system for generating differentially private synthetic tabular data by leveraging public domain-size information of attributes to avoid excessive privacy budget splitting, combined with mathematical programming for budget allocation and postprocessing methods (iterative non-negativity and consistency-aware normalization). Experiments show DPView achieves superior utility over prior parametric and non-parametric DP data synthesis approaches. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it was run in the study.
paper-dpview-differentially-private-synt.needs: Full text or citing sentence not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run as a baseline or only cited in related work.

paper-designing-hybrid-equipment-failure.summary: This paper proposes SmoteNC–ctGAN, a hybrid oversampling pipeline for equipment-failure diagnosis where rare, mixed-type (numerical and categorical) failure samples are first expanded with SmoteNC and then fed into a conditional tabular GAN to generate additional synthetic failure records before CatBoost classification. The authors present their own pseudocode and architecture equations (mode-specific normalization via Gumbel-softmax outputs and a condition vector) for the ctGAN stage rather than invoking a named package, and report it improves balanced accuracy versus SmoteNC-only and ctGAN-only baselines on machine failure datasets. CTGAN's conditional generator and mode-specific normalization are the algorithm the whole empirical pipeline rests on, reimplemented in the authors' own framework rather than run via the SDV library.
paper-designing-hybrid-equipment-failure.needs: Cannot fully confirm whether the described ctGAN equations are a from-scratch reimplementation or a wrapped call to the sdv-dev CTGAN class; no package name or import is mentioned, and the reported 'ELBO loss' hyperparameter is inconsistent with standard CTGAN's WGAN-GP loss, suggesting a custom build.

paper-fraudulent-account-detection-hiera.summary: This paper investigates hierarchical classification approaches (local per parent node and global, via CLUS-HMC) for detecting fraudulent financial accounts in a real, highly imbalanced dataset from a Brazilian fintech, and proposes Benford's Law-based features. To address class imbalance, the authors compare four oversampling techniques -- SMOTE, Borderline SMOTE, CTGAN, and TVAE -- across the classification schemes. CTGAN and TVAE are run directly (with parameters like generator_dim, discriminator_dim, and compress_dims/decompress_dims given) as two of several oversampling generators evaluated against SMOTE variants.

paper-improving-math-proficiency-predict.summary: This conference paper investigates whether data augmentation can improve a multi-class neural network's prediction of students' math proficiency using the PISA 2012 computer-based assessment dataset, focusing on the minority high-proficiency class. The authors compare SMOTE, a VAE, and CTGAN as data augmentation techniques, tuning CTGAN with several generator/discriminator dimension settings and reporting G-mean, recall and KS-distance for each. CTGAN, run via its published implementation with explicit generator/discriminator dimension hyperparameters, is one of three synthetic-data generators benchmarked, and its size-32/256 variants produced the best minority-class results.
paper-improving-math-proficiency-predict.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV's sdv-dev CTGAN package was used directly or a custom implementation, nor institutional affiliations.

paper-performance-ranking-recommender-sy.summary: This conference paper extends the SynEvaRec simulator to validate simulations of recommender-system/user interactions, proposing a procedure to check consistency of RS performance ranking across response matrices of varying sparsity. The empirical work centers on a recommender-system simulator rather than tabular data synthesis. The original SDV paper is cited among the references, with no indication in the available evidence that SDV software was run.
paper-performance-ranking-recommender-sy.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot verify whether SDV was actually used in the simulation pipeline or merely cited as prior work on synthetic data generation.

paper-security-user-profiles-2022.summary: Builds security user profiles from live data streams and detects anomalies against them, where working from real user traces raises the privacy problem the system is meant to serve. The generation engine is powered by the Synthetic Data Vault library, making SDV a runtime component of an operational pipeline rather than an offline step.

paper-semantic-enabled-architecture-audi.summary: This paper proposes WellFort, a semantic-enabled architecture for auditable, privacy-preserving data analysis, offering secure storage of sensitive personal data with explicit user consent and provenance/audit trails to support regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR) and reproducibility, particularly for small and medium organisations handling medical-type data. It surveys existing partial solutions including anonymisation and synthetic data generation approaches. The Synthetic Data Vault is named only in passing as one example approach to data anonymisation/synthesis, without being run or evaluated in the work.
paper-semantic-enabled-architecture-audi.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the related-work section beyond this single passing mention.

paper-sibyl-understanding-addressing-usa.summary: This paper presents Sibyl, a visual analytics tool designed to improve the interpretability and interactivity of local factor contributions for domain experts making high-stakes decisions, developed and evaluated through an iterative design process with child welfare screeners and validated via two user studies. For privacy reasons, the case data shown in the user study evaluation was synthetically generated rather than real. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, was run as the generator to produce this de-identified synthetic data for the study.

paper-tabular-transformers-modeling-mult.summary: This paper proposes TabBERT and TabGPT, transformer-based architectures for tabular time series that learn representations for downstream tasks and generate realistic synthetic tabular sequences, demonstrated on a synthetic credit card transaction dataset and a real pollution dataset. In its related-work discussion of static tabular data generation, it cites TGAN and CTGAN (Xu et al.) among a list of GAN/VAE-based generation methods, but does not run or engage with them experimentally. CTGAN and TGAN are only cited as prior art in a list of related synthetic tabular data generation methods.

paper-transfer-learning-thermal-comfort-.summary: This paper proposes a transfer-learning-based multilayer perceptron (TL-MLP-C*) that leverages thermal-comfort sensor data from multiple cities within the same climate zone to improve thermal comfort prediction, addressing the data-shortage problem in building HVAC research. It is evaluated on the ASHRAE RP-884, Scales Project, and Medium US Office datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. The SDV-family TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is named in a discussion of GAN-based techniques for handling imbalanced tabular data, but full-text search confirms it appears only in the reference list and is not run in the reported experiments.
paper-transfer-learning-thermal-comfort-.needs: The extracted citing sentences claim in-text use of 'TabularGAN [61]' for class-imbalance handling, which conflicts with the settled full-text finding that no SDV term appears outside the reference list; reference numbering (41 vs 61 vs 73) may be mismatched between citation extraction and the true bibliography, so it is unclear whether the paper actually ran the TGAN technique or merely cited it.

paper-imdpgan-generating-private-specifi.summary: This paper proposes imdpGAN, an information-maximizing differentially private GAN that simultaneously achieves privacy protection and learns controllable latent representations, evaluated on MNIST and CelebA. The work is a general privacy-preserving GAN framework unrelated to tabular data synthesis in its experiments. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is cited only in passing, in a list of generative-model works that mitigate data scarcity by generating tabular data, and is never engaged with further.

paper-survey-collection-machine-learning.summary: A comprehensive survey of data collection techniques for machine learning from a data-management perspective, covering data acquisition, labeling, and improvement of existing data/models across multiple research communities. It surveys and organizes techniques such as synthetic data generation, crowdsourcing, and weak supervision without proposing a new synthetic-data method itself. It cites the Synthetic Data Vault paper as an example of synthetic data generation used for its low cost and flexibility, and cites the TGAN paper in its reference list, without running either.
paper-survey-collection-machine-learning.needs: TGAN citation only confirmed via reference list; no in-text sentence quoting it was located in the provided passages.

paper-assessing-privacy-quality-syntheti.summary: This paper extends an earlier ESANN 2019 study by introducing new privacy metrics -- membership inference attack susceptibility and a discriminator-testing method -- to evaluate synthetic health data generators, focusing on a Wasserstein GAN variant the authors call HealthGAN compared against Gaussian Multivariate, Parzen Windows, Additive Noise, and differential-privacy baselines. The synthetic data vault's formulation for converting categorical features into numeric values between 0 and 1 is cited and adopted in the authors' own preprocessing pipeline to prepare data for HealthGAN, rather than by running SDV's code directly.
paper-assessing-privacy-quality-syntheti.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether SDV/RDT code was actually invoked or only its transformation concept was reimplemented.

paper-causal-inference-synthetic-pitfall.summary: Shows that a tabular synthesizer can pass distributional, privacy and train-on-synthetic-test-on-real checks while still distorting the average treatment effect, because prediction loss penalizes treatment-effect error only through an overlap-weighted term, so a generator can reproduce dominant observed outcomes while underlearning the intervention-relevant contrast; it formalizes the mismatch with sensitivity and loss-decomposition results and proposes a hybrid alternative that generates covariates with a generative model but fits the treatment and outcome mechanisms separately, then uses the result as a pre-analysis simulation engine for comparing OR, IPW, AIPW and TMLE estimators. CTGAN is one of the two generators the whole empirical program runs on, supplying both the fully generative arm and the covariate generator inside the proposed hybrid, and is credited in the related work for introducing conditional GANs with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling.

preprint-lab-tab-llm-augmented-2026.summary: This paper proposes LAB-Tab, a few-shot tabular data generation framework that fits a Bayesian network to a richer source-domain table, uses an LLM to propose plausible target-domain edges absent from the source graph, and calibrates these edges with a PPO policy before sampling target-domain tables. It is evaluated across six source-target distribution-shift scenarios built from US Census (ACS) tasks, where LAB-Tab is shown to outperform several baseline generators on distributional, utility, and dependency-preservation metrics. SDV's GaussianCopula and CopulaGAN synthesizers, along with CTGAN and TVAE, are run unmodified as baseline generators against which LAB-Tab's few-shot performance is benchmarked, with CTGAN singled out as the strongest baseline.

preprint-memisis-orchestrating-evaluatin.summary: Memisis is a demo tool that orchestrates synthetic tabular health-data generation and evaluation, combining existing synthesis libraries with an LLM-driven multi-agent pipeline that jointly negotiates utility, fairness, and privacy. On a schizophrenia misdiagnosis dataset it benchmarks six synthesizers spanning GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, and normalizing flows (including CTGAN and TVAE) across fidelity, fairness, and privacy metrics. SDV is invoked as one of two backend synthesis libraries (alongside Synthcity), supplying CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula-style synthesizers that are run and compared as evaluation subjects.
preprint-memisis-orchestrating-evaluatin.needs: Not fully clear which of the six evaluated synthesizers (CTGAN, TVAE, DDPM, PATEGAN, RTVAE, NFLOW) came from SDV versus Synthcity; assumed CTGAN/TVAE/GaussianCopula are SDV-sourced based on the citing sentence.

preprint-pate-tabtransgan-differentially.summary: Proposes PATE-TabTransGAN, a differentially private generative framework for tabular data that combines the Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles (PATE) mechanism with a Transformer-based student discriminator and a GNMax RDP accountant, aiming to jointly achieve formal DP guarantees and realistic inter-feature dependency modeling. It is evaluated on four tabular benchmarks (Adult, Breast, Cardio, Cervical) against PATE-GAN, DP-GAN, and DP-CTGAN, achieving best or tied-best AUROC across all datasets. The authors' own generator explicitly follows CTGAN's architecture, reimplementing its residual-block design and per-column activation scheme (sigmoid for continuous columns, Gumbel Softmax for categorical groups) rather than invoking the SDV library.
preprint-pate-tabtransgan-differentially.needs: DP-CTGAN baseline results are reproduced from a cited prior paper [8] rather than run by these authors, so only the generator's architectural debt to CTGAN is a direct engagement.

preprint-ramark-radioactive-watermarking.summary: This paper proposes RaMark, a radioactive watermarking method for synthetic tabular data that embeds a sinusoidal dependency directly into the underlying data distribution so the watermark survives even when an adversary retrains a new generative model on the watermarked data. It provides theoretical guarantees that removing the watermark necessarily degrades data utility, and evaluates radioactivity and robustness against seven state-of-the-art watermarking baselines across retraining and data-modification attacks. TVAE, one of the SDV-family's tabular synthesizers, is run as one of four retraining-attack generative models used to test whether RaMark's watermark survives regeneration.
preprint-ramark-radioactive-watermarking.needs: Unclear whether TVAE was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package or the authors' own reimplementation; no import statements or hyperparameter names given in the visible text.

paper-inter-column-logic-eval-2025.summary: Argues that the usual fidelity and utility measures miss whether a synthetic table preserves the logical relations that hold between its columns, and proposes three metrics for them - hierarchical consistency across nested geographic or organizational fields, mathematical and temporal dependency, and a distribution similarity index - then applies them to five generators on a real supply-chain dataset, finding that the latent-space models score well on distributional measures while failing the logical ones. CTGAN is one of the five evaluated generators, standing for the GAN category alongside SMOTE, TabDDPM, TabSyn and GReaT, and is reported across all the density, coverage, precision-recall and logical-consistency columns.

preprint-synthetic-generation-differenti.summary: This preprint proposes a differentially private synthetic tabular data generator based on Matrix Product States (MPS), a tensor-network model, extending it to handle categorical, integer, and continuous features while embedding gradient clipping and noise injection for formal privacy guarantees via Rényi DP accounting. The MPS model is benchmarked against classical generators (CTGAN, VAE, TVAE, PrivBayes) on fidelity and downstream classification metrics computed with the SDMetrics library, with MPS shown to outperform all baselines especially under strict privacy budgets. CTGAN is run as one of several comparison baselines (mis-cited to the 2018 TGAN paper by Xu and Veeramachaneni), and SDMetrics is used to compute the paper's fidelity scores.
preprint-synthetic-generation-differenti.needs: Reference [2] is actually Xu & Veeramachaneni's 2018 TGAN paper, but the text consistently labels and describes the model as 'CTGAN' -- likely a mis-citation rather than use of the original TGAN model; component/concept tags assume the intended model was CTGAN.

preprint-tabsym-generative-pipeline-smal.summary: This preprint proposes TabSyM, a modular generative pipeline for small, high-dimensional, multi-cohort omics tabular data that combines an extended diffusion model (TabDDPM), a Bayesian-optimization-guided task-aware sampling mechanism, and a Multi-Domain Adversarial Network for cross-cohort alignment, validated on gastric-cancer survival prediction from scRNA-seq data. The pipeline's headline generator is TabDDPM, not any SDV-family model. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited among the SDV-family works but the abstract gives no indication it was run or compared against in the reported experiments.
preprint-tabsym-generative-pipeline-smal.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed only in related work/references or actually used as a baseline generative model in experiments.

preprint-comprehensive-survey-augmentati.summary: This is a broad survey that unifies data augmentation techniques across five data modalities (image, text, graph, time-series, tabular) under a single inductive taxonomy based on relationships between and within instances. In its discussion of tabular data augmentation methods, it describes CTGAN as a GAN-based approach that focuses on the class-imbalance problem via a conditional generator for categorical columns, contrasting it with related methods like Table-GAN and ITS-GAN. CTGAN's conditional generator design is discussed in prose as prior work, not run or benchmarked in this survey.

preprint-credit-card-fraud-detection-202.summary: This preprint proposes a credit-card fraud detection pipeline that combines GAN-based synthetic data generation, feature engineering, and anomaly detection to address severe class imbalance in fraud datasets. The authors use the SDV library's CTGANSynthesizer, fitting it to the original transaction data with defined metadata and sampling conditions, to generate synthetic transactions that balance the dataset before training a classifier. SDV's CTGAN component, including its conditional generator and mode-specific normalization, is run directly as the synthetic data generator underlying the whole empirical pipeline.

preprint-cross-table-synthetic-tabular-2.summary: This preliminary study investigates whether synthetic tabular data can be reliably detected 'in the wild' across different generators, domains and table formats, proposing three cross-table baseline detectors and four evaluation protocols spanning increasing degrees of distribution shift. The synthetic datasets used to train and test these detectors are produced by four generators - TabDDPM, TabSyn, TVAE and CTGAN - reused from the authors' own prior work (Kindji et al., 2024) rather than freshly implemented here. CTGAN and TVAE, both introduced in the SDV-family CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, serve as two of the four synthetic-data sources whose outputs the detection models must distinguish from real data.
preprint-cross-table-synthetic-tabular-2.needs: The synthetic datasets from TVAE/CTGAN were generated in a prior paper (Kindji et al., 2024) not shown here; unclear whether that prior work used the sdv-dev package directly or a reimplementation.

preprint-graph-traffic-analysis-delay-20.summary: This paper builds MalTra, a new comprehensive vehicular traffic dataset for Malta, and combines it with the Q-Traffic dataset to benchmark ARIMA, STGCN and DCRNN models for traffic delay prediction, finding DCRNN outperforms STGCN. During data cleaning, the authors describe considering the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) to fill missing daily traffic records via its Gaussian and Conditional modelling options, but ultimately chose linear interpolation instead since the missing intervals were only five minutes apart.
preprint-graph-traffic-analysis-delay-20.needs: Confirm SDV was never actually executed on the dataset beyond being considered and described.

preprint-creating-high-quality-synthetic.summary: This preprint proposes a generative model for synthetic longitudinal electronic health record data based on generalized canonical polyadic (GCP) tensor decomposition, combined with sequential decision trees, copula methods, and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling, validated on MIMIC-III data for privacy-preserving data sharing. The abstract and available evidence describe the authors' own tensor-decomposition-based synthesizer rather than any SDV tool being run. The work cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper, apparently as related prior work on synthetic data generation.
preprint-creating-high-quality-synthetic.needs: No citing sentence or full text was obtained; only the OpenAlex reference link to sdv-dsaa-2016 confirms the citation. Cannot verify whether SDV is discussed, compared, or merely listed.

preprint-flaim-aim-synthetic-generation-.summary: This paper studies differentially private synthetic tabular data generation in the federated setting, proposing DistAIM and FLAIM as federated extensions of the central AIM graphical-model method, and an augmented FLAIM that mitigates client heterogeneity via a private heterogeneity proxy. The authors benchmark against federated DP-CTGAN baselines across seven tabular datasets, showing FLAIM matches DistAIM's utility with lower overhead. Two of the benchmark datasets, Census and Intrusion, are drawn from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), whose demo datasets are used purely as evaluation data rather than SDV's generative methods being run.
preprint-flaim-aim-synthetic-generation-.needs: SDV is used only as a source of two benchmark datasets (Census, Intrusion); no SDV synthesizer, metric, or schema object is run or discussed.

preprint-fedpnn-one-shot-federated-2023.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage one-shot federated learning framework: first a modified CTGAN generates synthetic non-i.i.d. tabular data at each client using noise drawn from two distributions instead of one, then a Federated Probabilistic Neural Network (FedPNN) combined with an evolving clustering method builds a global classifier from cluster centers aggregated at the server. The approach is validated on finance and medical datasets, with synthetic data quality judged via KSComplement and CStest scores. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional-vector generator architecture is directly modified (altering its noise generation) to produce the paper's core synthetic-data stage, and CTGAN is described using SDV-style quality metrics (KSComplement/CStest) for evaluation.

preprint-nyi-differential-privacy-statis.summary: This paper theoretically evaluates Rényi differential privacy of the randomness introduced by a synthetic data generation mechanism that samples from the mean vector and covariance matrix of an original dataset (equivalent to a Gaussian copula with normal marginals), deriving epsilon bounds under bounded and unbounded neighboring conditions. It positions this statistics-based approach against deep-learning-based generative parameter methods. CTGAN is named only in a related-work list of GAN-based tabular synthesis methods (alongside DPCTGAN, CTAB-GAN, CTAB-GAN+) and is never run or engaged with further.

preprint-machine-learning-sensors-2022.summary: A position/vision paper proposing 'ML sensors,' a paradigm that decouples ML processing from application processors at the hardware level to improve modularity, privacy, and integration in embedded ML systems. The authors motivate this design by discussing challenges like data drift and distribution shift between training and deployment environments. SDV is cited only in passing as one of several references for 'synthetic data methods' that could help address training-production data mismatch, with no experiments or implementation described.

repo-oreilly-mlops-with-databricks.summary: Code accompanying an O'Reilly title on running MLOps workflows on Databricks, built around a hotel-booking example. SDV produces the data the whole book operates on: the data processor imports `Metadata` and `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and `sdv==1.24.0` is pinned, so every later pipeline stage consumes SDV output.

repo-gen-ai-for-researchers.summary: Course material introducing generative AI for academic research, covering generative models, prompt engineering and responsible use. Its data-generation unit teaches SDV: `synthetic_data_generation.ipynb` loads a demo table with `sdv.datasets.demo.download_demo`, describes it with `SingleTableMetadata` and fits a `CTGANSynthesizer`. SDV's demo loader and conditional GAN are run as the worked example for synthetic data.
